A.title: Ash Slope Marker
A.text: A post at the foot of the slope with a rag tied to it. Go up the shaded side. The sunward ash is still hot a hand's width down.

Y.title: A Caravan, Buried
Y.text: Wagon ribs, an iron strongbox, a trader's scale. The strongbox is empty. The owner scratched his tally on the wagon wall until the sand covered it.

R.title: The Shield Stone
R.text: A flat stone with a hand pressed into it. Lay your own hand there and the heat of the dunes eases. The caravan masters did this daily.

G.title: Trader's Rhyme
G.text: Walk by night and rest by day. Keep the dune-crest on your right. If the wind goes still, then say your name. If it answers, run.

M.title: Cold Ground
M.text: The dunes are cooler than they were. My grandfather says the war was fought here and the sand is its ash. Cooling, he says, not cold.

O.title: Watch Post
O.text: An old sentry post on the high ridge. From here you can see three miles of dune and anything that moves on it. Wait for a clear hour.

U.title: Water Count
U.text: Ledger line: eight skins out, six left. Day four. The well on the map is dry. Mark it so the next man does not walk to it.

X.title: Wind Mark
X.text: The wind wipes the dunes clean every night. Cut your mark deep or it is gone by morning. Mine says only: I was alive until day nine.
